Having used virtual reality:

It's amazing in first person. Seriously, one of the first VR games I've ever played was this helicopter game- it was super simple and probably had the least impressive 3D cityscape in a game this side of the N64- the developer had tossed the game together in a few days for the event he was displaying it at! Yet, it was an unforgettable experience. I really felt like I was soaring, and hadn't noticed the line that formed behind me- time seemed to melt away.

It's weird- a game doesn't need super-realistic graphics to look good in VR- it just has to run smoothly.

But don't knock VR until you've tried it, it's pretty awesome.
that is a relief. i would rather wait for vr to mature a little than rush it and be disappointed but it sounds like it's further along than i thought.

I've played some Half Life 2 on the Oculus DK2 and played with some demos on the GearVR. The problem I had with the DK2 was that the low resolution, filtered through the lenses, caused really bad screen door effect. The head tracking and 3D were awesome.

The 2 things that grabbed me with the GearVR were video clips from a helicopter flying over locations in Iceland and stills from the Mars rover. The helicopter shots were breathtaking. I could look through the whole scene - sky, mountain, river, meadow. The Mars shots were static, but 360 degrees. I could see the horizon, the rover, the tire tracks on the ground. I was blown away looking at the stars from the surface of another planet.

John Carmack talks about "conversion on contact" with VR. Somebody might not really get it from reading articles and watching videos, but once they experience it, they understand the impact.
